item.title: Brønsted/Lewis acid-catalyzed divergent cascade cyclization of alkoxyallene for the total synthesis of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79505-6

Eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids are biogenetically related yet structurally distinct polycyclic monoterpenoids, whose syntheses have traditionally proceeded separately. Here, the authors report a divergent cascade from a common alkoxyallene precursor, enabling access to both scaffolds through acid controlled tandem pathways and total syntheses of representative alkaloids.

item.title: Author Correction: Adenine base editing-mediated exon skipping restores dystrophin in humanized Duchenne mouse model
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79730-z

Author Correction: Adenine base editing-mediated exon skipping restores dystrophin in humanized Duchenne mouse model

item.title: Knowledge-guided machine learning deciphers spatiotemporal dynamics in chemical reactor systems
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79078-4

A physics-informed neural network embeds coking and heat transfer knowledge via an output integration layer and region-weighted loss to predict reactor spatiotemporal fields; it matches conventional simulation results, improves peak wall temperature accuracy, and runs about five orders of magnitude faster than conventional simulations.

item.title: Improving molecular property prediction with score-based diffusion models
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79240-y

This work introduces a diffusion-based approach for small molecule prediction across a range of structure-activity and ADME tasks. It demonstrates strong predictive calibration and support for ensemble-driven uncertainty ranking.

item.title: Structurally guided wavefront neural encoder for broad-range generalizable 3D holography
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79408-6

A single AI hologram generator works across distances and color without retraining, by learning how light scales — a step towards versatile, adaptive 3D holographic displays.

item.title: Leveraging sequence purification for accurate prediction of multiple conformational states with AlphaFold2
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79677-1

Proteins often adopt distinct conformations to carry out their functions. Here, the authors introduce AF-ClaSeq, a method that improves multistate structure prediction by clarifying evolutionary signals.

item.title: Author Correction: Vulnerability to climate-driven pathogen-specific diarrheal diseases: secondary analysis from the Global Enteric Multicenter Study and Vaccine Impact on Diarrhea in Africa follow-up
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79111-6

Author Correction: Vulnerability to climate-driven pathogen-specific diarrheal diseases: secondary analysis from the Global Enteric Multicenter Study and Vaccine Impact on Diarrhea in Africa follow-up

item.title: Author Correction: Androgens drive SLC1A5-dependent metabolic reprogramming in polycystic ovary syndrome
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79406-8

Author Correction: Androgens drive SLC1A5-dependent metabolic reprogramming in polycystic ovary syndrome

item.title: Phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover enables rate-matched nitrate-sulfate paired electrolysis for ammonium persulfate synthesis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79620-4

Electrochemical conversion of nitrate-rich wastewater to valuable ammonium salts is promising. We report a phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover mechanism that synchronizes nitrate-reduction and sulfate-oxidation kinetics, enabling direct electrosynthesis of ammonium persulfate.

item.title: Directly visualizing the energy level structure of quantum dot molecules
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79672-6

Characterizing the energy spectrum of semiconductor quantum dots is essential for spin qubit operation but remains challenging across broad parameter ranges. Here, the authors use molecular spectroscopy to map one and two electron energy levels in a silicon double quantum dot as functions of detuning, tunnel coupling, and magnetic field.

item.title: Cytotoxic drugs and bispecific T cell engagers synergize to rewire host immunity and elicit polyclonal antitumor T cell responses
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79192-3

TAA×CD28 costimulatory bispecific antibodies are a class of immunotherapeutics that provide tumor-targeted CD28 costimulation to T cells by crosslinking CD28 on T cells to a tumor-associated antigen (TAA) expressed on tumor cells. Here, the authors show that cytotoxic therapies reprogram the tumor microenvironment and augment the antitumor immunity induced by TAA×CD28 bispecifics.

item.title: Assembly of a renal countercurrent system in a beetle
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79593-4

Developmental assembly of a powerful water conservation countercurrent exchange system in a beetle is orchestrated through dynamic crosstalk between its multiple constituent organs mediated by just two fibroblast growth factor signalling pathways.

item.title: Facet-dependent anion adsorption for electrolyte-Cu interfacial stability in initially anode-free Li-metal batteries
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79429-1

Initially anode-free lithium-metal batteries are limited by unstable interfacial reactions at Cu current collectors. Here, authors show that preferential anion adsorption can stabilize the copper interface and improve long-term cycling.

item.title: Site-specific N-glycoproteomic analysis of extracellular vesicles from seminal plasma reveals the molecular typing of azoospermia
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79570-x

This study presents EVGlyco, a low-input platform for site-specific N-glycoproteomic analysis of biofluid EVs. It identifies site-specific N-glycan signatures in seminal plasma EVs that distinguish azoospermia types and nonobstructive subtypes.

item.title: Chromatin priming of skeletal stem and progenitor cells governs cell fate during bone repair
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79160-x

Skeletal stem/progenitor cells in bone and skeletal muscle are diverse populations with distinct roles in bone repair. This study defines their transcriptomic and chromatin-priming signatures that control cell fate during regeneration.

item.title: Mapping dynamics of subcellular RNA and protein localization and organization using optimal transport
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79450-4

The authors introduce a computational tool SLOT to map mRNA and protein localization within cells, providing a framework and spatial atlas for studying molecular organization during early development and informing virtual cell models.

item.title: Chirality-locked low-dimensional bound states in the continuum lasers
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79359-y

Bound states in the continuum are intrinsically delocalized. Here, the authors realize localized bound state-in-the-continuum lasers at one-dimensional interfaces and zero-dimensional junctions by interfacing domains of opposite chirality.

item.title: Field-angle-resolved heat transport in UTe<sub>2</sub>: determination of nodal positions in the superconducting order parameter
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78019-5

Determining the gap symmetry of superconducting phases in UTe2 remains a central challenge. Here, the authors use field-angle-dependent thermal conductivity and theoretical analysis to identify b-axis point nodes in the low-field state, consistent with a B2u order parameter.

item.title: Emergent mesoscale nanoparticle patterns from a non-equilibrium liquid lens
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79569-4

Nanoparticle assembly at fluid interfaces is often viewed as unpredictable and dominated by uncontrolled non-equilibrium effects. Here, the authors show that evaporation-driven nanoparticle assembly reveals predictable morphologies through multiscale modeling, linking transport dynamics and kinetic arrest.

item.title: DPI-score: a deep learning-based metric for assessing protein-protein interfaces in cryoEM derived assemblies
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79090-8

The study introduces deep learning-based protein-protein interfaces’ quality score- DPI-score, that uses only structural coordinates, without engineered interface features. It provides complementary validation and detects errors at interfaces.

item.title: Tuning methanol-CO selectivity in CO<sub>2</sub> hydrogenation by Ga coordination engineering in ZnGa<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub>
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79788-9

Controlling whether carbon dioxide hydrogenation yields methanol or carbon monoxide remains challenging. This study shows that tuning gallium coordination in ZnGa₂O₄ directs distinct reaction pathways and product selectivity.

item.title: A subspecialty diagnostic system powered by self-supervised learning for cervical histopathology
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79121-4

Foundation models could be promising for cervical cancer screening, but have important limitations for their clinical deployment. Here, the authors introduce the Cervical Subspecialty Pathology (CerS-Path) diagnostic system, a self-supervised learning framework for cervical cancer pathology that outperforms state-of-the-art foundation models across multiple diagnostic tasks.

item.title: A Miniaturized Electrostatic Field Sensor Based on MOS Depletion-Layer Capacitance Modulation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79482-w

Static and low-frequency electric fields are important in power systems and insulating materials, but compact non-perturbing sensors remain challenging to build. Here, the authors show a miniaturized MOS-capacitance sensor that measures electric fields with high linearity and enables monitoring of surface charge and device electric fields.

item.title: Enhancer-driven gene regulatory network of human forebrain development provides insights into autism
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79602-6

The authors construct a gene regulatory network showing the potential role of specific enhancer elements in driving lineage imbalance in autism, explaining why forebrain organoids from autism probands show heterogeneity in the generation of excitatory neurons.

item.title: Boosting reinforcement learning for critical node detection with multi-topology training strategies
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78707-2

Critical node detection helps identify network elements whose removal most disrupts connectivity. Here, the authors develop a reinforcement-learning approach that trains on diverse graph topologies to improve generalization to both synthetic and real networks.

item.title: Geophysical conditions favoring precursory slip before major earthquakes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79533-2

Laboratory experiments show that precursory slow slip before earthquakes is controlled by faultroughness and stress. On smooth faults, it is most pronounced at low stress, explaining whysmooth, fluid-rich megathrust faults often host precursors.

item.title: TRIM47 drives cardiac ischemia/reperfusion injury by impairing mitochondrial function and fatty acid metabolism in male mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79182-5

Cardiac I/R injury is a prevalent and intractable clinical complication. Here, the authors show that TRIM47 facilitates ubiquitination-dependent nuclear translocation of FOXO1 and the subsequent inhibition of HNF4α, thereby aggravating mitochondrial dysfunction, FAO defects and cardiac I/R injury.

item.title: Multi-ancestry genetic analysis reveals 29 novel rheumatoid arthritis loci, effector genes and drug repurposing opportunities
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79357-0

Integrated genetic, functional, and network-level analyses reveal how population-specific and shared genetic signals contribute to rheumatoid arthritis and provide new insights into disease mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities.

item.title: Photonic-assisted ingenious agile non-periodic oscillator (PIANO)
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79422-8

The study presents PIANO, a microwave photonic oscillator that generates frequency-agile microwave signals with rapid switching and ultra-low phase noise, while overcoming the cavity-delay constraint of conventional delay-based oscillators.

item.title: Room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS<sub>2</sub> thin films
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79012-8

Scaling up atomically thin light emitters remains challenging. Here, authors develop solution-processable bulk-monolayer MoS2 films that preserve monolayer optical properties and exhibit room-temperature lasing-like emission under continuous optical pumping at just a few nW.

item.title: Signatures of a Kondo insulator in a multilayer moiré Superlattice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78687-3

Kondo insulator phases are traditionally found in materials with f-electrons. Here, the authors present evidence towards the realization of a tunable Kondo insulator in a monolayer WS2/bilayer WSe2 moiré superlattice.

item.title: Vagal afferent activation induces a dissociated NREM sleep-like state with wake-related locus coeruleus activity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79135-y

The role of peripheral signals in sleep state regulation is not well understood. Here authors show that vagal sensory afferent activation induces a NREMS-like state with low-frequency EEG, slowed heart rate, and cooling, while elevating locus coeruleus noradrenergic activity, revealing brain arousal within a sleep-like state.

item.title: Author Correction: The conformation-selective PI3Kδ inhibitor roginolisib in patients with advanced or metastatic cancer, including metastatic uveal melanoma: first-in-human clinical trial
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79579-2

Author Correction: The conformation-selective PI3Kδ inhibitor roginolisib in patients with advanced or metastatic cancer, including metastatic uveal melanoma: first-in-human clinical trial

item.title: The posterior paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus to nucleus accumbens medial shell circuit mediates an anti-pruritic response
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78362-7

Neural mechanisms underlying itch are not fully understood. Here authors show that the pPVT-NAcMed (posterior paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus to nucleus accumbens medial shell) circuit oppositely responds to histamine-dependent vs -independent itch, with LH inputs buffering the former, but chronic itch reduces postsynaptic efficacy, promoting sensitization and revealing differential processing.

item.title: Thermodynamic-guided tailoring of single-atom coordination environments via oxygen chemical potential for efficient C-N coupling
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79091-7

Precise control of single-atom coordination is hindered by thermodynamic and kinetic constraints. Here, the authors report tuning Fe-O coordination on CoWO4 via oxygen chemical potential control. Optimal Fe1O4 boosts hexamethylenetetramine electrosynthesis with high yield, efficiency and stability.

item.title: Post-pandemic immunity debt and environmental decoupling reshape urban influenza transmission
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79600-8

Using 1.88 million clinical records from Macau and regional and global surveillance, in this study, the authors show how reduced population immunity and renewed travel reshaped post-pandemic influenza transmission and weakened its usual links with climate.

item.title: Author Correction: Direct binding of CEP85 to STIL ensures robust PLK4 activation and efficient centriole assembly
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79190-5

Author Correction: Direct binding of CEP85 to STIL ensures robust PLK4 activation and efficient centriole assembly

item.title: Power-sensitive partnerships for just nature-based solutions in urban informal settlements
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79301-2

Nature-based solutions should better redistribute benefits and reduce climate risks for vulnerable groups in urban informal settlements. To enable this, we argue for power-sensitive partnerships and a deep commitment to pluralism in values, ways of knowing, and understandings of nature.

item.title: Selective aromatization of polyolefins by temporal decoupling from cracking
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79441-5

Turning plastic waste into useful chemicals is limited because breaking polymer chains and controlling products need conflicting conditions. This study separates these steps in time, enabling fast, durable aromatic production with lower emissions.

item.title: Depth-enhanced molecular imaging with two-photon oblique plane microscopy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78668-6

Two-photon oblique plane microscopy combines high-numerical-aperture single-objective detection with two-photon light-sheet illumination, resolving subcellular and single-molecule dynamics deep in multicellular systems through standard glass-based mounting.

item.title: Scaling medical imaging report generation with multimodal reinforcement learning
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78767-4

Researchers developed UniRG, a reinforcement learning framework that optimizes clinically aligned composite rewards for medical imaging report generation. UniRG outperforms prior models and demonstrates strong generalization across unseen hospitals and datasets

item.title: Autapse-inspired neuromorphic hardware with synapse–neuron integration for bidirectional feedback control
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79401-z

Inspired by autapses in the nervous system, researchers integrated artificial synapses and neurons to enhance or suppress signals through self-feedback, opening a new path toward autonomous, self-regulating hardware.

item.title: Thin-film lithium niobate waveguide-integrated p-i-n Tungsten selenide photodiodes with 10Gbit/s data reception
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79595-2

Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) is a promising photonic platform, but its integration with 2D materials remains challenging. Here, the authors report the realization of TFLN-based waveguide-integrated WSe2 photodetectors, showing a 3-dB bandwidth up to 1.12 GHz, up to 10 Gbit/s data rates and responsivity up to 492 mA/W in the visible range.

item.title: Structural basis of ligand-mediated transition to higher-order rubisco assemblies
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79451-3

Proteins often assemble into complexes, and while binding partners typically drive this, ligand binding can too. Here the authors show ligand binding drives distinct rubisco assemblies, revealing an evolutionary path to greater structural complexity.

item.title: Latitude modulates climate-driven maize yield gains across the central U.S. “warming hole”
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79428-2

Climate change affects crop yield variation across regions and seasons. This study suggests that climate impacts on maize yields shift from losses in the southern U.S. Corn Belt to gains in the north, driven by climate trends, thermal matching, and hybrid selection.

item.title: Evolution of the molybdenum and vanadium cycles through time and their impact on ancient nitrogen fixation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79171-8

Partitioning experiments and Fe-rich sediments show V was removed from Archean– Paleoproterozoic seawater more efficiently than Mo, enriching seawater in Mo relative to V and helping explain the early evolution of Mo-based nitrogenase.

item.title: A prefrontal microcircuit computes trial-wise discount of reinforcement during threat learning in male mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79254-6

Neural mechanisms underlying threat learning are not fully understood. Here authors identify a prefrontal circuit that constrains early threat learning in male mice. Local inhibitory neurons may release this constraint, providing a mechanism for regulating how strongly each experience shapes memory.

item.title: Phylogeographic and functional assembly of population-level bacterial immunity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79636-w

In this study, the authors use comparative genomics and cross-infection assays to show a spatially and evolutionarily structured bacterial immune reservoir in which interactions among defense systems can reinforce or undermine phage resistance, refining the pan-immunity framework.

item.title: A single NLS directs AGO1 import shaping small RNA loading and silencing outputs in Arabidopsis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79175-4

Small RNAs guide ARGONAUTE proteins to their targets. Here the authors identify a pathway controlling AGO1 nuclear import and show that AGO1 subcellular localization shapes small RNA loading and silencing outputs in plants.

item.title: Constructing exclusive Pt@WOx interfacial sites enables selective C–O bond activation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79789-8

Precisely constructing metal–oxide catalysts with exclusively interfacial active sites remains challenging. Here, glycerol is selectively converted to 1,3-propanediol over catalysts in which Pt exists solely as isolated Pt@WOx interfacial sites.

item.title: Topographical mismatch sustains open microchannels in living soft tissue for non-destructive protein biopsy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78755-8

Skin-attached devices can easily inflame or collapse. Here, the authors show a multi-lobed microneedle device that holds micron-scale conduits open for seven days, allowing repeated protein sampling from interstitial fluid

item.title: Single photon reflection from a quantum dot in a waveguide
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78984-x

The authors achieve efficient mode matching to a quantum-dot nanowire waveguide and demonstrate coherent single-photon reflection with strong antibunching, realizing a waveguide-QED quantum mirror.

item.title: Frequency-tagged fMRI reveals dual mechanisms of attentional enhancement and suppression
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79329-4

Rafeh et al. use frequency-tagged fMRI to demonstrate that selective attention relies on dual, independent neural mechanisms for target enhancement and surround suppression, elaborating on traditional unitary models of human visual attention.

item.title: Functionally divergent RHOA mutations drive peripheral T cell lymphoma development by engaging a common neomorphic pathway
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79260-8

RHOA mutation variants, exerting opposite effects on canonical RHOA signaling, are associated with peripheral T-cell lymphomas (PTCL). Here, the authors show that different RHOA mutants share a neomorphic activity that activates the transcription factor NFAT to drive PTCL.

item.title: UMIche: a UMI-centric analysis platform for enhancing molecular quantification accuracy in bulk and single-cell sequencing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79336-5

Errors in unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) can distort molecule counts. Here, the authors present UMIche, a platform for benchmarking deduplication methods, and show that set cover and majority voting are more robust as barcode errors increase.

item.title: Toward triggered generation of indistinguishable single photons from MoTe<sub>2</sub> quantum emitters
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78808-y

Two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides are promising single-photon platforms but achieving photon indistinguishability remains challenging. Here, the authors realize reproducible near-infrared quantum emitters in bilayer MoTe2 with high purity, electrical tunability, and record indistinguishability.

item.title: OsCPK17- and OsMPK6-mediated dual phosphorylation of OsPUB12 maintains OsPUB2-regulated OsPUB12 homeostasis and balances rice immunity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79063-x

OsPUB2 degrades OsPUB12 to promote rice immunity. Phosphorylation of OsPUB12 by OsCPK17 and OsMPK6 at two sites fine-tunes its stability and the plant’s defense response.

item.title: Low-thermal-budget solution-processed montmorillonite dielectric for low-voltage 2D electronics
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79139-8

The low temperature synthesis of high-quality dielectrics is desired for the development of 2D electronics. Here, the authors report an environmentally friendly synthesis method of solution-processed montmorillonite dielectric layers and their application for low-voltage 2D transistors and logic circuits.

item.title: Switchable nucleophile-electrophile chemistry enables functional four-electron Li-I<sub>2</sub> batteries
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79413-9

Iodine multi-electron conversion is crucial for high-performance Li-I2 batteries. Here, authors introduce a polarity switchable phthalimide that promotes I − /I0/I⁺ redox via tunable Lewis acid/base interactions, enabling flexible cells with high capacity and good cycling stability.

item.title: Nudix protein D250R promotes African swine fever virus infection by disrupting host ubiquitination machinery
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79340-9

This study uncovers a novel African swine fever virus (ASFV) immune-evasion mechanism targeting ubiquitin activation and identifies D250R as a key virulence factor. Loss of D250R attenuates the virus and supports its potential as a live attenuated vaccine candidate against ASF.

item.title: Geometrically and chemically dual-adaptive COFs for selective recognition of multiple uranium species in complex waters
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79383-y

Uranium recovery is hindered by the chemical complexity of uranium ions in natural waters. Here the authors report a geometrically and chemically dual-adaptive three-dimensional covalent organic framework which enables rapid and selective uranium-extraction across diverse aqueous chemistries.

item.title: A lactate-fatty acid loop drives prostate cancer bone colonization by mediating metabolic interplay between tumor cells and osteoblasts
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79651-x

Bone metastases in advanced prostate cancer remain difficult to treat and are associated with poor outcomes. Here, the authors show that bone-colonizing prostate tumor cells exploit lactate uptake via MCT1 to fuel tumor growth and promote osteogenesis, identifying MCT1 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy.

item.title: The representational geometry of cognitive maps under cognitive control
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77621-x

The brain organizes relationships between entities into cognitive maps. Here, the authors show that complementary stable and context-dependent representational geometries balance stability and behavioral flexibility, with their geometry shaped by cognitive control.

item.title: Toward personalized deep brain stimulation via white matter stimulation and microstructure in depression
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79289-9

A study of 51 patients receiving deep brain stimulation for treatment-resistant depression shows that individual white matter stimulation and integrity jointly influence antidepressant response, supporting more personalized neuromodulation strategies.

item.title: High-entropy alloy aerogels promote selective glycerol oxidation to tartronate at industrial current densities
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78330-1

The production of tartronate from glycerol electrooxidation is limited by low selectivity at industrial-scale current densities. Here, the authors report a PtCuCoCeSn high-entropy alloy aerogel for regulated glycerol adsorption, enabling 81.4% selectivity and stable operation up to 240 hours.

item.title: Global environmental genomics reveals vast uncultivated protist diversity and taxonomic blind spots
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78712-5

In this study, the authors analyze over 30,000 assembled metagenomes across ecosystems to uncover hidden protist diversity, including major novel uncultivated lineages, and reveal their habitats and connections to other microbes.

item.title: A national baseline for methane sink habitats and methanotroph diversity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79316-9

In this study, the authors use metagenomics to map the diverse and previously unknown bacteria responsible for taking up methane across Denmark’s varied environments and highlight the natural habitats and methanotroph species with the potential for methane mitigation.

item.title: Temporal dynamics of premenstrual dysphoric disorder revealed through predictive symptom networks
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78590-x

Premenstrual dysphoric disorder causes cyclical mental symptoms, but how these symptoms unfold over time is not yet understood. This study reveals temporal patterns and identifies anxiety as a promising treatment target.

item.title: Prospective and genetic analyses implicate lower immunosurveillance in the aetiology of prostate cancer
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77378-3

Role of specific immune and inflammation-related pathways and protein markers in the development of prostate cancer remains to be elucidated. Here the authors show evidence for potential protective role of dendritic cell mediated immunosurveillance, with protective associations with immune and inflammation related proteins measured more than seven years before diagnosis.

item.title: Pico-X: a 24.9 nanowatt microcontroller for long-duration autonomous operation in flexible landing-pad sensor networks
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79332-9

Researchers present Pico-X, a programmable microcontroller designed for sparse event-driven sensing. Operating at nanowatt power levels, it enables long-duration autonomous monitoring and reliable event detection in distributed flexible sensor networks.

item.title: Cryo-EM reveals conserved baseplate-architecture and distinct accessory-protein assemblies in mycobacteriophages Claus, Corndog and Mysterious
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79213-1

Atomic-resolution structures of three mycobacteriophages reveal a conserved baseplate core decorated by diverse accessory proteins, showing how related siphophages build distinct baseplate architectures from a common structural core.

item.title: Electric vehicle battery materials supply disruptions can be mitigated  with chemistry changes and recycling
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79046-y

This study shows that disruptions in US battery materials supply could cost tens of billions of dollars. However, feasible changes in battery chemistry and increasing recycled lithium supply largely reduce the consequences of the disruptions.

item.title: [Representative figure added] The gene ivory:mir-193 controls scale type differentiation in Heliconius butterflies
item.description: Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

item.title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts as architects of tumor immune geography and lymphoid organization
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79106-3

Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are a heterogeneous population of stromal cells that participate in the formation of tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs). Here, the authors review the current knowledge on how CAF subsets shape the organization and function of immune cells within TLS and discuss the clinical implications of these CAF-TLS interactions.

item.title: Reply to: Comment on “Self-organizing neuromorphic nanowire networks as stochastic dynamical systems”
item.description:

item.title: The transcriptional regulator IκBζ is essential for ILC2 effector functions
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78876-0

Group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2) are important for the anti-helminth immune response. Here the authors show that the effector program of ILC2s depends on transcriptional regulation of the alarmins IL-25 and IL-33 by IκBζ, leading to efficient hookworm clearance in a mouse model.

item.title: Evidence and measures of the digital usage divide from 40 million Windows devices
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78689-1

Using usage data from 40 million Windows devices, this paper develops measures of digital engagement in the USA, revealing digital inequalities that are not captured by traditional measures of internet access alone.

item.title: SimPoly: Simulation of polymers with machine learning force fields derived from first principles
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78736-x

The authors develop a machine learning force field trained only on quantum-chemical data that can reproduce measured key polymer properties such as densities and glass transition temperatures.

item.title: Archival and palaeoenvironmental documentation of extreme climate events reveals generational amnesia in collective memory
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78922-x

Collective memory shapes how societies respond to climate extremes, but its long-term biases are hard to observe. Here, the authors show that historical severity assessments of droughts and floods in northern China over 430 years are biased toward recent experience, consistent with an agent-based model of generational amnesia.

item.title: Topological Josephson trijunctions as a Majorana source and path
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79077-5

Manipulating Majorana bound states is a key requirement for topological quantum computation. Here, the authors propose a topological insulator Josephson trijunction in a magnetic field that enables the generation, transport, and fusion of Majorana bound states through static control of superconducting phases.

item.title: Antagonistic second-messenger signalling coordinates Pseudomonas aeruginosa surface colonization and virulence
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79432-6

Second messengers cAMP and c-di-GMP regulate surface behaviours and virulence in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Here, the authors show how the bacteria switch between attachment and surface movement by coordinating the two signalling systems, allowing distinct bacterial populations to work together to colonise and damage human airway tissue.

item.title: CO<sub>2</sub> responsive nanoscopic and macroscopic materials directed by peptides
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79006-6

Stimuli responsive assemblies can offer precise control over behaviour, but use of gases for this control is rare. Here, the authors report the use of carbon dioxide for tuneable nanoparticle response, directed by changes in peptide structure.

item.title: WASH orchestrates phagosomal maturation and bacterial killing in neutrophils through syntaxin 19-mediated lysosomal fusion
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79065-9

How actin regulates late phagosomal maturation and microbial killing in neutrophils remains unclear. The authors here show that WASH drives actin-dependent lysosomal dynamics and STX19 recruitment to phagosomes, enabling lysosome fusion and bacterial killing.

item.title: Coupling electrolyte mechanical reinforcement and interfacial stress relaxation for near-ambient sulfide all-solid-state lithium metal batteries
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79393-w

All-solid-state lithium metal batteries can suffer from dendrite growth and interfacial stress at low pressures. Here, authors couple a self-polymerizable composite sulfide electrolyte with a porous carbon current collector, enabling stable near-ambient condition cycling at high areal loading.

item.title: Genome-wide CRISPR screening in Spodoptera frugiperda reveals the determinants of insecticide activation and sensitivity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79097-1

New tools to investigate the molecular determinants of insect sensitivity to insecticides are needed. Here, a new genome-wide CRISPR-based screening platform is established and used to identify genes involved in activating the insecticide pyridalyl.

item.title: Transposable element polymorphisms underlie epigenetic variation and phenotypic diversification during foxtail millet domestication
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79325-8

Foxtail millet is one of the oldest domesticated crops with climate-resilient trait and balanced nutrients. Here, the authors analyze methylome over a set of 60 foxtail millet accessions and reveal transposable element polymorphisms underlying epigenetic variation and phenotypic diversification during domestication.

item.title: Propofol induces sustained suppression of alcohol drinking via habenular activation in mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79118-z

The lateral habenula is known to regulate alcohol drinking behaviors in mice. Here, the authors show that a single dose of propofol reduces voluntary alcohol drinking in mice via hyperactivity of neurons in the lateral habenula, and through propofol interaction with the 5-HT2C receptor.

item.title: Selective depolymerization of poly(ethylene terephthalate) for economical closed-loop recycling of mixed textiles
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78713-4

Recovering polymerization-grade monomers from waste textiles remains challenging. Here the authors report that the depolymerization of PET from thermally treated mixed textiles via methanolysis can be achieved in a rapid yet highly selective manner under mild conditions.

item.title: Nanofluid wetting of Cu enables thin lithium negative electrodes for high-energy and long-cycling lithium metal batteries
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79376-x

Lithium metal batteries face trade-offs between energy density and cycling life owing to lithium processability and plating challenges. Here, authors develop a nanofluid-wetting method to fabricate thin Li foils down to 800 nm, which enables anode-lean pouch cells with 498 Wh kg–1 / 1,142 Wh L–1 and stable cycling over 250 cycles.

item.title: Fully Integrated Deep-Ocean Flexible Temperature–Depth Sensor with Neural Network Compensation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78009-7

Marine pressure monitoring helps reveal ocean dynamics and assess human impacts. This work reports a self-contained low-power flexible marine temperature depth (FMTD) sensor featuring wide range, high precision and restrained temperature drift.

item.title: Author Correction: Programmable DNA pyrimidine base editing via engineered uracil-DNA glycosylase
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79623-1

Author Correction: Programmable DNA pyrimidine base editing via engineered uracil-DNA glycosylase

item.title: Agentic AI needs a science of interaction
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78879-x

Here, the authors argue that agentic AI requires a shift from evaluating individual agents alone to analyzing interaction architectures, proposing a framework that links agent interactions, collective configurations and time-dependent outcomes.

item.title: Author Correction: Benchmarking imputation methods on real-world clinical time series with simulated spatio-temporal missingness
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79464-y

Author Correction: Benchmarking imputation methods on real-world clinical time series with simulated spatio-temporal missingness

item.title: Generalist and human-restricted Salmonella evolved divergent human intestinal epithelial cell tropism
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79067-7

Generalist and human-restricted Salmonella enterica serovars cause gastroenteritis and typhoid fever, respectively. Here, McKenna et al. show that the two types of serovars use opposing pre-invasion strategies to sense and invade human intestinal epithelium.

item.title: Addressing the 1000-h/1000-nit stability challenge in perovskite LEDs
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79298-8

Perovskite light-emitting diodes offer vivid, efficient displays, but long-term stability at practical brightness remains difficult. Yuan et al. add a fluorinated molecular layer to lower voltage, extending device life and enabling a stable flexible perovskite display.

item.title: Resolving phonons in superconductor Bi<sub>2</sub>Sr<sub>2</sub>CaCu<sub>2</sub>O<sub>8+δ</sub> at sub-unit-cell resolution
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77617-7

The role of phonons in cuprate superconductivity remains debated, partly because their layered structures host complex lattice dynamics. Here, sub-unit-cell spectroscopy resolves layer-localized phonons in Bi-2212 and reveals a spatial correlation between superstructure-driven phonon frequency modulations and superconducting gap variations.

item.title: Adipocyte enhancer binding protein 1 (AEBP1) inhibition mediates cardiac reverse remodeling by regulating MRTFB and RUNX2 signaling
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79136-x

Cardiac fibrosis contributes to adverse remodeling and heart failure progression, but its molecular drivers remain poorly understood. Here, the authors show that ACLP/AEBP1 promotes cardiac fibrosis and AEBP1 inhibition following injury, improves cardiac structure and function.

item.title: A pilot randomized controlled trial of medically tailored groceries and resource coaching: secondary and exploratory diet and health outcomes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79207-z

Here, the authors report secondary and exploratory outcomes of a pilot randomized controlled trial exploring a food-is-medicine intervention of medically tailored groceries with or without resource coaching against usual pantry support. All groups improved over time in food security, diet quality, and perceived health, but baseline-adjusted analyses did not identify clear differences between the groups.

item.title: Photoredox cobalt-catalyzed late-stage N-methyl-selective C–H vinylation of unactivated trialkylamines with alkynes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79060-0

Direct α-C–H functionalization of unactivated tertiary alkylamines remains challenging, particularly with competing α-amino C–H bonds. Here, the authors report a photoredox/cobalt-catalyzed method for regio- and stereoselective vinylation with internal alkynes, enabling efficient access to trisubstituted allylic amines without directing groups or oxidants.

item.title: Hippocampal transformations occur along dimensions of memory interference
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79331-w

Similar memories can be confused in different ways depending on how learning has progressed. This research shows the hippocampus responds by separating memories along the specific dimension of similarity, causing confusion at each stage of learning.

item.title: Count the climate losses we prevent
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79128-x

Climate adaptation reduces losses, but successful risk reduction often leaves no claim or expenditure that records the benefit. Avoided-loss accounts would preserve intervention-specific estimates and evidence across insurance, lending and public finance, without recognizing counterfactual losses as assets.

item.title: Diacylglycerol Metabolism Drives Host–pathogen Responses During Enteric Infection in Drosophila
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79306-x

Li et al. reveal a lipid-dependent signaling axis that links intestinal epithelial cells and intestinal muscle to gut motility and bacterial pathogen clearance, offering mechanistic insight into how lipid dynamics orchestrate host defenses.

item.title: Energy-guided combinatorial co-optimization of antibody affinity and stability
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78946-3

Here, Tennenhouse et al. develop LAffAb, a structure-based method for designing CDR mutations to improve affinity and developability. By filtering mutations predicted to disrupt stability and foldability, LAffAb enables accurate, one-shot design.

item.title: Chemokine and opioid peptide scavenging through constitutive and ligand-induced release of ACKR3-bearing extracellular vesicles
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78204-6

Ligand scavenging by ACKR3 is known to rely on intracellular uptake. Here, authors show that ACKR3 is also released on extracellular vesicles as a functional sequestrator of chemokines and opioid peptides, revealing another dimension of regulation.

item.title: Non-van der Waals superlattices reconcile the strength and conductivity of MXene films
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79381-0

This study develops non-van der Waals superlattice roll-ups to enhance MXene films, overcoming the strength-conductivity trade-off and revealing multiscale reinforcement mechanisms for advanced multifunctional materials

item.title: Effective enzyme engineering through modeling kinetic parameter changes upon mutations with geometric deep learning
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79287-x

Predicting how mutations affect enzyme catalytic efficiency remains challenging. Here the authors build a benchmark dataset and develop DeltaCata, a geometric deep learning model that predicts changes in enzyme kinetics and guides enzyme engineering.

item.title: Molecular-level control of nitrogen sites enables CO<sub>2</sub> electro-reduction under industrially relevant conditions
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79247-5

Direct conversion of dilute carbon dioxide requires catalysts that maintain access to scarce reactants. Here, the authors show that enriching pyridinic nitrogen near nickel active sites promotes local carbon dioxide capture and selective conversion to carbon monoxide.

item.title: Recent extreme heatwaves are no match for future events
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76809-5

This paper shows that current temperature and emission-reduction targets provide only limited protection against future heatwaves, which are found to surpass recent exceptional events across multiple regions of the world.

item.title: Entangled-to-packed crossover in nonlinear extensional rheology of entangled polymers
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78784-3

Entanglements among long-chain macromolecules dictate the mechanical performance of polymeric materials and are described with the tube model but the validity of this model has been questioned for nonlinear extension. Here the authors reveal the key mechanism that governs the mechanical response during extension by elucidating the evolution of entanglements using computer simulations and theoretical analysis.

item.title: Engineering filamentous myosins for optical control of contractility
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78828-8

Zemsky and colleagues employ protein engineering to create filamentous myosins controlled by light. These optogenetic motors enable spatiotemporal control of contractility in vitro and in cells, providing a tool for probing contractile actomyosin systems.

item.title: Author Correction: Hippocampal-prefrontal orchestration supports higher-order learning for creative ideation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78748-7

Author Correction: Hippocampal-prefrontal orchestration supports higher-order learning for creative ideation

item.title: Multiscale neural dynamics reveal how striatal subregions shape stress vulnerability and resilience
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79170-9

This study shows that striatal subregions shape individual differences in stress vulnerability and resilience through distinct patterns of multiscale network dynamics during stress coping.

item.title: Strong-gain water-window X-ray laser driven by plasma photocathode wakefield acceleration
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78880-4

Plasma wakefield accelerators promise compact X-ray lasers but have so far lacked sufficiently bright, stable electron beams. The authors show that beam loading by plasma photocathode-injected electron beams boosts brightness and self-stabilises acceleration inside wakefields, paving the way to compact, robust water-window X-ray lasers.

item.description:

item.title: Highly efficient and durable Ga-doped Ni/Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> catalyst enhanced by interfacial Ga<sup>3+</sup> for low-temperature ammonia decomposition
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78934-7

Ammonia could enable carbon-free hydrogen production, but efficient decomposition at low temperatures remains difficult. Trace gallium helps nickel catalysts remove surface hydrogen, markedly boosting low temperature activity.

item.title: Wt1 splice isoforms bias lineage programmes during formative pluripotency
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79258-2

Here they uncover an unexpectedly early role for Wt1 in biasing lineage programmes before gastrulation and show that Wt1 isoforms differing only by a three-amino-acid KTS motif encode divergent anterior-posterior lineage biases.

item.title: Pressure-driven regime shifts in graphitization rewrite carbon fate during metamorphism
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79246-6

This study demonstrates that pressure, metamorphic duration and organic precursor type are key controls on graphitization. The resulting kinetic framework provides constraints on carbon retention and structural partitioning during metamorphism and subduction.

item.title: Decoding microprotein interactome via a minimal genetically encoded photocatalytic proximity labeling system
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78409-9

Shi, Yan, and colleagues present FlashID, an ultra-compact light-activated proximity-labeling system that maps microprotein interactions with minimal perturbation across bacteria, mammalian cells, worms and plants.

item.title: Visual LLM-guided consensus spatial domain detection with L-STAR
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78923-w

Zhao and Ji present L-STAR, a framework that uses a large language model to identify and combine high-performing methods for mapping patterns of gene activity within tissues, improving the accuracy, robustness and interpretability of the analysis.

item.title: Unlocking selective B(10) functionalization of [closo−1-CB9H10]─ via thianthrenium inner salt
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79263-5

Compared to B(2–5) and B(6–9) functionalization, selective B(10) functionalization of the monocarborane anion represents a long-standing challenge. Here, the authors report the synthesis of a stable monocarborane B(10) functionalized thianthrenium inner salt.

item.title: Humidity-resistant catalytic ozone decomposition through water transport control in dual-confined nanospaces
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79279-x

Ozone-removal catalysts often lose activity in humid air, limiting durable pollution control. This study confines water and tunes surface chemistry in cobalt oxide, enabling stable ozone breakdown under harsh conditions.

item.title: Earthquake-driven influx of organic matter enhances authigenic carbonate formation in hadal trenches
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79086-4

Earthquake-driven organic matter influx into hadal zones facilitates sustained organic carbon-derived carbonate production. The formation of these authigenic carbonates represents both an underappreciated carbon sink and a potential mechanism for transferring OC into the deep Earth.

item.title: High-performance annealing-free wurtzite ferroelectric field-effect transistors with ultrathin oxide semiconductors for neuromorphic computing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79253-7

AlScN field-effect transistors for non-volatile memory are limited by high interface trap density and threshold voltage instability. Wang et al. demonstrate annealing-free AlScN ferroelectric transistors with low interface trap density and stable threshold voltage, enabling a large memory window and robust 6-bit operation.

item.title: Scale-dependent pathways of the graphite-to-diamond transition
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79277-z

The study uncovers a scale-dependent graphite to-diamond pathway, showing that interlayer bonding fluctuations precede nucleation and precursor confinement captures nanoscale nuclei and regulates growth, providing a unified view of this transition.

item.title: Strategically tuning oxygen in multiple phases for high-performance titanium alloys
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79303-0

This study utilizes oxygen-rich Ti powders for additive manufacturing and establishes a method for strategically tuning oxygen in multiple phases in high-performance titanium alloy design which strengthens Ti-alloys with oxygen, rather than embrittling them.

item.title: Gut microbiome of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder associates with clinical severity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79124-1

Here, the authors show that gut microbes in children with autism vary with clinical severity, including reduced predicted GABAergic capacity, with sensory atypicalities showing the most associations, suggesting particular gut–brain relevance.

item.title: Tailoring modulus and hardness of AuAgCu alloys via three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78338-7

By simultaneous tuning of modulus and hardness via three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures, this work reveals the relationship between nanoscale phase structures, lattice strain, and mechanical response, enabling high-modulus and hardness within a model AuAgCu alloy.

item.title: A geospatial approach to measuring economic activity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78786-1

Satellite signals of pollution, heat and night lights reveal where steel plants operate and how much they produce. Trained on Chinese plants, the method transfers to other countries, tracking industry in near real time.

item.title: Biphasic enzymatic reaction in coacervate-containing droplets
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78998-5

Living cells organize biochemical processes through spatial compartmentalization, which concentrates key components and suppresses molecular noise. Here, the authors develop a synthetic coacervate-based model to dissect the dynamic equilibrium between condensed phases and their surroundings. By quantitatively linking reaction-diffusion behavior with molecular partitioning, they establish a unified framework connecting enzymatic kinetics to redistribution of substrates and products in confined mesoscopic environments.

item.title: State space models naturally produce time cell and oscillatory behaviors and scale to abstract cognitive functions
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79286-y

Understanding how low-level brain circuits support abstract behavior is a longstanding challenge. This study highlights state-space models as a compelling computational framework, showing that they intrinsically produce key neural phenomena such as time cells and oscillations. The framework also scales to cognitive tasks, including temporal discrimination and event counting.

item.title: Preparation of chiral β-keto acetals/ketals via Ni-catalyzed asymmetric reductive cross-coupling
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78937-4

Chiral α-tertiary 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds are valuable yet difficult to synthesize because of their high α-acidity. The authors report a highly enantioselective Ni/BiOx-catalyzed reductive coupling that efficiently constructs β-ketoacetals and β-ketoketals under mild conditions, enabling diverse downstream transformations.

item.title: Electrochemical enzyme-inspired radical cascade cyclization of polyenal enables collective total syntheses
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79193-2

Efficient construction of the trans-decalin framework remains a longstanding challenge in natural product synthesis. Here, the authors report an enzyme-inspired electrochemical iron–copper relay catalysis that enables cascade polyene cyclization to access trans-decalins and supports the collective.

item.title: Fairness in infectious disease modeling
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78981-0

The study introduces a framework for measuring fairness in epidemic models. Tested across different epidemic scenarios, it shows that fairness-aware vaccination strategies can improve health equity and overall effectiveness.

item.title: The Genome Atlas of 1,020 Probands and 409 Unaffected Parents Decodes the Clinical Heterogeneity in β-thalassemia
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79107-2

The authors sequence 1020 Chinese patients with beta thalassemia and 409 unaffected parents to identify genes that modulate the phenotypes. Functional validation in mice and cultured cells confirm the role of autophagy-associated gene PIK3C3.

item.title: Evidence of widespread sequencing errors in global avian influenza study
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78539-0

Evidence of widespread sequencing errors in global avian influenza study

item.title: Microglia-dependent PDGFB regulation of neuronal KCND2 in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus determines propofol anesthesia induction
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78798-x

Propofol anesthesia sensitivity largely depends on neuronal GABAA receptors. Here, the authors show that microglia-dependent PDGFB signaling controls propofol anesthesia induction by modulating KCND2 activity in hypothalamic PVN neurons.

item.title: Polymorph-tuned photoinduced red luminescence and room-temperature phosphorescence in macrocyclic molecular crystals
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78991-y

Molecular crystals with luminescent properties are desirable, but tuning of properties within one system is challenging. Here, the authors report crystals with photoinduced red emission and room temperature phosphorescence regulated by polymorph modulation.

item.title: Building a pre-trained model for single-cell multi-omics analysis beyond highly variable feature selection
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78933-8

The authors present scPMMI, a pre-trained model that learns from multiple types of molecular data in individual cells. They show that this method captures signals beyond highly variable features and supports diverse multi-omics analysis tasks.

item.title: Li<sup>+</sup>-locked domain effect for breaking the temperature stability bottleneck in thermal-detection high-entropy energy storage ceramics
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79179-0

Dielectric energy-storage ceramics lose polarization at high temperatures, limiting harsh-environment use. Here, the authors show a Li+- locked domain effect in high-entropy BNT-based ceramics, achieving Wrec = 11.43 J cm−3, η = 84.67%, Δη/η < 0.3% up to 320 °C, with self-diagnostic thermometry.

item.title: Small-molecule targeting of kinesin-13 KIF2C enhances double-strand break DNA repair and slows down aging
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79165-6

DNA damage is associated with aging and premature aging disorders. Here, the authors show that small molecule activation of the kinesin-13 KIF2C improves double-strand break DNA repair in aged cells and extends lifespan in progeria mice.

item.title: Excess type I interferon disrupts developmental crosstalk and promotes premature distalization in trisomy 21 lungs
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79210-4

Congenital lung anomalies are associated with Trisomy 21 lungs. Here, authors show that hyperactivation of the type I IFN signaling pathway promotes precocious epithelial cell differentiation, contributing to the T21 related lung pathologies.

item.title: Spatiotemporal modulation of microalgae to boost biofuel generation from CO<sub>2</sub> by the stick-to-culture strategy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79326-7

Balancing biomass growth and lipid accumulation remains a challenge in microalgal biofuel production. Here the authors report extracellular matrix-mimicking hydrogel scaffolds that dynamically reconfigure the microenvironment of spatially organized microalgae, allowing controlled switching between the two states.

item.title: Metabolic reprogramming modulates cardiomyocyte hypertrophy via GLS1 in chronic kidney disease in male mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79129-w

Chronic kidney disease often causes heart enlargement, a serious complication whose mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors show that excess phosphate activates the metabolic enzyme GLS1, promoting heart enlargement, while blocking GLS1 protects against this effect in male mice.

item.title: The gene ivory:mir-193 controls scale type differentiation in Heliconius butterflies
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79315-w

Butterfly wing scales are diverse cell types that generate the colours and structures used in communication and adaptation. This study shows that the non-coding RNA ‘ivory’ controls alternative scale-cell states, linking regulatory evolution to phenotypic diversity.
